2609.11865.title: Epistemic orientation predicts legislative effectiveness among members of the US Congress
2609.11865.paper_summary: Truth and evidence-based communication provide important foundations for democratic governance, accountability, and collective decision-making. Prior work shows that evidence-oriented language in US congressional floor speeches has declined since the mid-1970s, alongside broader changes in legislative productivity and polarization. This study shifts the analysis from congressional sessions to individual members of Congress to examine whether epistemic orientation varies systematically across legislators and whether it relates to political behavior and legislative effectiveness. Using the Evidence-Minus-Intuition (EMI) score, we measure the relative prevalence of evidence-oriented versus intuition-oriented language in congressional floor speeches and Twitter posts. We link these measures to legislator-level data on ideology, institutional position, communication context, and Legislative Effectiveness Score (LES). The results show that more ideologically extreme members use less evidence-oriented language on the congressional floor. EMI also exhibits cross-platform consistency with members who use more evidence-oriented language in floor speeches also being more evidence-oriented on Twitter, although EMI is lower on Twitter overall. Finally, EMI in congressional speeches is positively associated with individual legislative effectiveness, even after accounting for ideology and extensive political, institutional, demographic, topical, and communication volume controls. These findings suggest that evidence-oriented language is not only an aggregate feature of congressional discourse but also a meaningful attribute of individual-level legislative communication and effectiveness.
2609.11865.paper_summary_zh: 真相和基於證據的溝通為民主治理、問責制和集體決策提供了重要基礎。<lb/>先前的研究顯示，自1970年代中期以來，美國國會的發言中以證據為導向的語言有所減少，這與立法生產力和兩極化的更廣泛變化相關。<lb/>本研究將分析重心從國會會議轉移到個別國會成員，以檢視知識取向是否在立法者之間系統性變化，以及它與政治行為和立法效能的關係。<lb/>使用證據減直覺（Evidence-Minus-Intuition, EMI）分數，我們測量國會發言和推特發文中以證據為導向的語言與以直覺為導向的語言的相對盛行程度。<lb/>我們將這些測量結果與立法者層級的意識形態、機構地位、溝通背景和立法效能分數（Legislative Effectiveness Score, LES）數據聯繫起來。<lb/>結果顯示，意識形態極端的成員在國會發言中使用較少的以證據為導向的語言。<lb/>EMI在不同平台之間也顯示出一致性，使用更多以證據為導向語言的成員在國會發言中也在推特上表現得更具證據導向，儘管推特上的EMI整體較低。<lb/>最後，國會發言中的EMI與個別立法效能呈正相關，即使在考慮意識形態及廣泛的政治、機構、人口統計、主題和溝通量控制後也是如此。<lb/>這些發現表明，以證據為導向的語言不僅是國會話語的一個總體特徵，也是個別層級立法溝通和效能的一個有意義的屬性。
